Equate the curve and line equations:
$$-\frac{2}{x} = ax + 3a \implies -2 = ax^2 + 3ax \implies ax^2 + 3ax + 2 = 0$$

For the line and curve to intersect at two distinct points, the quadratic must have two distinct real roots, requiring $\Delta > 0$:
$$\Delta = (3a)^2 - 4(a)(2) > 0 \implies 9a^2 - 8a > 0$$

Factorise and state the solution set:
$$a(9a - 8) > 0$$
$$a < 0 \quad \text{or} \quad a > \frac{8}{9} \quad \left(\text{or } (-\infty, 0) \cup \left(\frac{8}{9}, \infty\right)\right)$$
